audit.why: Marked EVEN at 7/10 against a 48.53% win rate over 614 games — the largest sample in this slice and genuinely a coin-flip lane that tilts to Trundle after level 6. The level chart (Skill x5, Graves x2) matches.
Spike order is right: his level 2-3 Quickdraw/Smoke window, your level 6 Subjugate flip, your Iceborn Gauntlet first item. Subjugate stealing True Grit armor is correctly identified as the swing.

audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen is described three separate times as blinding you ('makes your Q Chomp miss entirely', 'blinding your Chomps and autos', 'your bite and W autos are blinded'). It does not blind. Separately, the single biggest early-lane interaction is absent: New Destiny fires four bullets that cannot pass through units, so Graves's shells are absorbed by minion bodies.
audit.why: Riot text for Smoke Screen: 'creates a cloud of smoke that reduces sight range. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' No blind, no miss chance — and Chomp is a targeted melee cast that cannot miss regardless. Riot text for New Destiny: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which cannot pass through units.'
audit.corrected: Rewrote the smoke as a nearsight you walk out of, and added minion-body absorption as the level-1 farming rule.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json P New Destiny, W Smoke Screen

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags this matchup for having no cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere, and it is right — every line says 'track Quickdraw' with no number and no ordering.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s but refunds on every basic attack that lands, so it is almost never the punishable cooldown. Smoke Screen at 26/24/22/20/18s is the real one, and Collateral Damage is 100/80/60s.
audit.corrected: Made Smoke Screen's 26s the cooldown you actually wait out, and said explicitly why Quickdraw is not worth waiting for.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json E, W, R cooldowns and E description

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing warns that your own Pillar of Ice is a detonation surface for End of the Line.
audit.why: End of the Line 'detonates after 1 second, or after colliding with terrain'. Pillar of Ice becomes impassable terrain. Dropping E between you and Graves hands him an early trigger.
audit.corrected: wants.you[2] now says to place Pillar behind Graves, never between you.

edits.before: Graves has two shotgun shells that hit harder than you expect at level 1 — don't walk into his auto range just to land a Q Chomp; farm at the tip of Q distance and let him come to you. At level 2 he will Quickdraw in, unload both shells, then dash back out, and his smoke makes your Q Chomp miss entirely if he plants it on your face before the trade. Don't commit a full trade into his smoke window — let the blind expire, then respond. Your passive King's Tribute heals from minion deaths, so you're not losing HP as fast as it looks; you are stable but not winning these early exchanges.
edits.after: Graves hits harder than you expect at level 1, but New Destiny fires four bullets that cannot pass through units — last-hit with a minion body between you and most of the pellets never arrive. At level 2 he will Quickdraw in, unload both shells, then dash back out. Smoke Screen does not blind you; it cuts your sight range, and Chomp is a targeted cast that lands anyway — walk out of the cloud instead of freezing in it. Your passive King's Tribute heals you off every minion death, so you are stable early — just not winning these exchanges.

edits.before: With Q and W up he plants Smoke Screen on your face, blinding your Chomps and autos before dashing out — you lose this trade cleanly.
edits.after: With Q and W up he plants Smoke Screen on your face — it nearsights you, it does not blind you, but he kites out of the cloud and wins the trade.

edits.before: Level 4 to 5 is where the matchup flattens out: Graves wants to reload and poke you, you want to force an extended fight. Every time he uses Quickdraw offensively to get close for a double-barrel, drop Frozen Domain immediately and start biting his AD — the longer the trade goes inside your W, the worse it is for him. At 6, Subjugate changes everything. He has moderate armor from Quickdraw stacks and his own item path; hitting R on him strips that armor directly onto you mid-duel, and inside your W you become nearly unkillable. Force the all-in the moment Subjugate is up — don't wait.
edits.after: Level 4 to 5 is where the matchup flattens out: Graves wants to reload and poke, you want an extended fight. Smoke Screen is the cooldown worth waiting on at 26s rank 1 — Quickdraw refunds time on every auto he lands, so it is always back and never worth baiting. Every time he Quickdraws in for a double-barrel, drop Frozen Domain immediately and start biting his AD; the longer the trade runs inside your W, the worse it gets for him. At 6, Subjugate strips his True Grit armor straight onto you mid-duel. Force the all-in the moment R is up — don't wait.

edits.after: True Grit armor off Quickdraw plus a 26s Smoke Screen — he can burst you down before Frozen Domain heals any of it back.

edits.before: Smoke Screen your face before the all-in so your bite and W autos are blinded

edits.before: Kite backwards with ranged autos and reload burst before you can close the gap again

edits.after: - Graves Smoke Screen: matchup-defining — 26s at rank 1. Quickdraw refunds on every auto, so wait out the smoke instead.

notes: Packet says 48.53 / 614 for this one, matching disk exactly — the only matchup in the slice where they agree. The blind claim was in three separate fields and is the highest-value correction here: Graves has had no blind on Smoke Screen for many years, and Chomp is a targeted cast that could not miss even if he did.
